legend: Santa Claus has n tangerines, and the i-th of them consists of exactly ai slices. Santa Claus came to a school which has k pupils. Santa decided to treat them with tangerines.

However, there can be too few tangerines to present at least one tangerine to each pupil. So Santa decided to divide tangerines into parts so that no one will be offended. In order to do this, he can divide a tangerine or any existing part into two smaller equal parts. If the number of slices in the part he wants to split is odd, then one of the resulting parts will have one slice more than the other. It's forbidden to divide a part consisting of only one slice.

Santa Claus wants to present to everyone either a whole tangerine or exactly one part of it (that also means that everyone must get a positive number of slices). One or several tangerines or their parts may stay with Santa.
Let bi be the number of slices the i-th pupil has in the end. Let Santa's joy be the minimum among all bi's.
Your task is to find the maximum possible joy Santa can have after he treats everyone with tangerines (or their parts).
input: The first line contains two positive integers n and k (1 ≤ n ≤ 106, 1 ≤ k ≤ 2·109) denoting the number of tangerines and the number of pupils, respectively.
The second line consists of n positive integers a1, a2, ..., an (1 ≤ ai ≤ 107), where ai stands for the number of slices the i-th tangerine consists of.
output: If there's no way to present a tangerine or a part of tangerine to everyone, print -1. Otherwise, print the maximum possible joy that Santa can have.
note: In the first example Santa should divide the second tangerine into two parts with 5 and 4 slices. After that he can present the part with 5 slices to the first pupil and the whole first tangerine (with 5 slices, too) to the second pupil.
In the second example Santa should divide both tangerines, so that he'll be able to present two parts with 6 slices and two parts with 7 slices.
In the third example Santa Claus can't present 2 slices to 3 pupils in such a way that everyone will have anything.

input.ai: 第一行包含两个正整数 n 和 k（1 ≤ n ≤ 106，1 ≤ k ≤ 2·109），分别表示橘子的数量和学生的数量。
第二行包含 n 个正整数 a1， a2， ...， an（1 ≤ ai ≤ 107），其中 ai 表示第 i 个橘子由多少瓣组成。

output.ai: 如果无法给每个人一个橘子或橘子的一部分，则输出 -1。否则，输出圣诞老人可能获得的最大快乐值。

note.ai: 在第一个样例中，圣诞老人应将第二个橘子分成两部分，分别包含 5 瓣和 4 瓣。之后，他可以将包含 5 瓣的部分送给第一个学生，并将完整的第一个橘子（同样包含 5 瓣）送给第二个学生。
在第二个样例中，圣诞老人应将两个橘子都分开，这样他就能得到两份包含 6 瓣的部分和两份包含 7 瓣的部分。
在第三个样例中，圣诞老人无法以一种让每个人都得到至少一些橘子瓣的方式，将 2 瓣橘子分给 3 个学生。

legend.ai: 圣诞老人有 n 个橘子，其中第 i 个橘子恰好由 ai 瓣组成。圣诞老人来到了一所学校，这所学校有 k 名学生。圣诞老人决定把橘子分给他们。
然而，橘子的数量可能太少，无法保证每名学生至少得到一个完整的橘子。因此，圣诞老人决定将橘子分成若干部分，以免有人感到不满。为此，他可以将一个橘子或任意已有的部分分成两个大小尽可能相等的更小部分。如果他想分割的部分包含奇数瓣，那么分割后其中一部分将比另一部分多一瓣。禁止分割只包含一瓣的部分。
圣诞老人希望给每个人分发一个完整的橘子，或某个橘子恰好一个部分（这也意味着每个人都必须得到正数瓣）。可以有一个或多个橘子或它们的部分留在圣诞老人手中。
设 bi 表示第 i 名学生最终得到的瓣数。令圣诞老人的快乐值为所有 bi 中的最小值。
你的任务是求出圣诞老人将橘子（或它们的部分）分给所有人后，可能获得的最大快乐值。
